stewards.name: Visa
stewards.role: Writes the specification and Product Terms, onboards agents, hosts the key store and signs the ID Token.

implementers.name: Cloudflare
implementers.role: Development partner (co-developed TAP with Visa) and edge verifier; planned Agents SDK support and managed rules (announced 2025-10-24).

implementers.name: Akamai
implementers.role: TAP support across Akamai Cloud (announced 2025-12-17). On 2026-06-15 Akamai announced an agentic security framework for its Bot & Agent Control products that cites TAP for agents in payment environments but names no TAP-specific setting; Visa named Akamai among the providers supporting live merchant implementation on 2026-07-02.

implementers.name: lastminute.com, Frasers, Cleverbridge, BrickDepot
implementers.role: Merchants in Visa's live European agent transactions (2026-07-02).

implementers.name: eDreams ODIGEO (eDreams, Opodo, GO Voyages, Travellink)
implementers.role: Said it is using TAP and the Agentic Directory to recognize verified agents (2026-07-03, secondary report).

implementers.name: Worldpay
implementers.role: Acquirer that announced collaboration with Visa and Cloudflare on TAP at launch.

implementers.name: Launch feedback partners
implementers.role: Adyen, Ant International, Checkout.com, Coinbase, CyberSource, Elavon, Fiserv, Microsoft, Nuvei, Shopify, Stripe and Worldpay gave feedback; not a list of deployments. Adyen, Ant International (as Antom), Checkout.com, Fiserv and Stripe are named in Visa's Agentic Ready acceptance release of 2026-11-17, and Nuvei in its European and Asia Pacific lists of 2026-11-18, as participants testing readiness rather than TAP deployments.

implementers.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce Connect
implementers.role: Visa on-ramp that accepts agent payments initiated through TAP, MPP, ACP and UCP. Visa and Lianlian DigiTech announced a live business-to-business purchase through it on 2026-11-18; Visa has announced no general availability.

implementers.name: mppx (Tempo, wevm)
implementers.role: MPP SDK with a TAP identity prover and verifier (mppx/extensions/identity/tap since 0.16.0, 2026-10-28; request attestation before).

implementers.name: BILL
implementers.role: Agent provider: the BILL Payment Agent, registered using TAP and the Agentic Directory, pays buyer-approved invoices on supplier portals with tokenized credentials (live pilot announced 2026-10-20, no counts published).

implementers.name: Billtrust
implementers.role: Supplier-portal platform that uses TAP to recognize, authenticate and admit the BILL Payment Agent (live pilot announced 2026-10-20).

implementers.name: Airwallex
implementers.role: Agentic Ready acceptance participant that Visa says is working to build TAP into each interaction (2026-11-17); a stated plan, not a deployment.

implementers.name: J.P. Morgan Payments
implementers.role: Named only in Visa's Perspectives copy of the 2026-11-17 release: testing how agentic network tokens and associated TAP signals move across merchant, acquiring and network infrastructure.

implementers.name: Lianlian DigiTech
implementers.role: Agent provider on Visa Intelligent Commerce: its LoopXPay agent, registered in the Agentic Directory, made a live business-to-business purchase (announced 2026-07-24), and its XWorker agent, also registered there, bought through Intelligent Commerce Connect (2026-11-18). Neither release says the agents sign with TAP, and neither gives counts.

sdks.name: mppx
sdks.note: MIT; mppx/extensions/identity/tap provides a TAP prover and verifier since 0.16.0 (2026-10-28), replacing mppx/attestation/tap; since 0.19.0 the prover takes a key pair, and the changelog lists no TAP change from 0.19.1 to 0.21.1. Not a Visa package. Version as of 2026-11-21 (published 2026-11-19).

sdks.name: @visa/cli
sdks.note: Visa Crypto Labs CLI under Visa's own license. Release candidates from 5.0.0-rc.335 (2026-09-18) sign TAP requests; the latest release, 4.0.1, does not. Release candidate as of 2026-11-21 (rc.491, published 2026-11-20 21:05 UTC, still with TAP request signing); latest still 4.0.1.

sdks.name: mpp-card
sdks.note: Visa's MPP card SDK under Visa's own terms.

sdks.name: visa/trusted-agent-protocol (sample code)
sdks.note: Python and Node.js sample, no published package; last commit 2025-10-28.

sdks.name: visa/ai workspace packages (@visa/api-client, @visa/mcp-client, @visa/token-manager)
sdks.note: VIC clients, not published on npm as of 2026-10-19.

metrics.metric: Merchants named as live with TAP
metrics.definition: Merchants Visa named in its live European agent transactions.
metrics.caveat: No total count of verifying merchants is published (Visa newsroom and developer pages, 2026-11-21); the Agentic Ready acceptance releases of 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-18 count participants testing readiness, not merchants that verify TAP.

metrics.metric: European issuers with live agent purchases
metrics.definition: Issuers named in Visa's release; the text says over 30.
metrics.caveat: VIC program metric, not TAP traffic. It counts issuers whose cardholders' agents completed live purchases, unlike Visa's later counts of issuers participating in Agentic Ready.

metrics.metric: Initial participants in Agentic Ready for acceptance
metrics.definition: Merchants, payment service providers, acquirers, business-to-business suppliers and commerce platforms that Visa says the acceptance phase launched with.
metrics.caveat: Participants testing readiness, not live deployments or TAP verifiers. The European (more than 85) and Asia Pacific (50+) releases of 2026-11-18 list overlapping names, and Visa does not reconcile the three counts.

metrics.definition: Issuers across 45 markets that Visa says participate as they prepare for agentic commerce.
metrics.caveat: Self-reported VIC program figure for participating issuers, not issuers with live agent purchases or TAP traffic. Visa does not say whether its regional counts of 2026-11-18 (more than 40 European issuers; over 100 issuers in 10 Asia Pacific markets) are included, so the figures are not added.

metrics.definition: Visa's own description of completed agent transactions.
metrics.caveat: Self-reported VIC figure; named transactions are pilots or first transactions.

metrics.metric: Partners working with Visa on agentic commerce
metrics.definition: Visa said over 30 build in the VIC sandbox and over 20 agents and enablers integrate directly.
Visa internal data on bot-initiated transactions.

metrics.metric: AI-driven traffic to US retail sites
metrics.definition: Adobe year-over-year figure for July 2025 (published August 2025), cited in Visa's launch release of 2025-10-14.
metrics.caveat: Adobe figure quoted by Visa; month-level date only.

costs.value: None stated in the Product Terms
costs.caveat: The license is revocable, and Visa can change the specification at any time; implementers must apply each update within six months.

costs.value: Free in sandbox; production fees on request from Visa
costs.caveat: No public production price. Read live on 2026-10-11 and cited from the archive of 2026-10-03; Visa's VIC developer docs, public again on 2026-11-14, state no fees.

costs.whoPays: No agent-specific fee published; ordinary acquiring fees apply as far as published
costs.caveat: Evidence of absence from Visa's pages and two secondary reviews. Visa's public rules (since 2025-10-18, current edition 2026-10-24) set no agent-specific fee, and its US interchange schedule (2026-10-24 edition, like the April 2026 one) has no agentic category; treat agent purchases as ordinary tokenized card-not-present payments until Visa publishes otherwise.

costs.value: Cloudflare's signed-agent field needs an Enterprise plan with Bot Management; no TAP-specific price
costs.caveat: Plan pricing is not public. The field covers Web Bot Auth agents; Cloudflare does not document whether TAP verifications set it.
